profile.headline: Ex-NASA JPL Senior Full-Stack Engineer & Software Architect | Specializing in Scientific Data Systems for Climate, Earth, & Environmental Science | Integrating Technical & Creative Design | Seeking Remote Opportunities
profile.summary:
After 16 incredible and impacting years my time at NASA JPL concluded in October, 2025. I am now eagerly seeking my next challenge where I can apply my skills in full-stack development and software architecture to mission-driven problems in the climate, earth, and environmental sciences. I'm looking for full-time or part-time remote work.

I specialize in a crucial translation: turning complex Earth science data into intuitive, scalable web applications that empower scientific discovery. My career is built on a unique foundation where rigorous technical architecture meets the principles of visual storytelling and human-centered design.

I have led the end-to-end development of mission-critical software, from initial UI/UX design and front-end development (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Leaflet.js) to backend engineering (Python, Flask) and database architecture (MySQL). My approach is defined by a blend of skills: the analytical mindset of an engineer to build robust, high-performance systems, and the empathetic eye of a visual artist and writer to craft interfaces that are not only functional but also clear, engaging, and accessible. 

I am now seeking to apply this distinct skill set to urgent challenges in climate, earth, and environmental sciences. My goal is a fully remote Senior Engineer or Software Architect role with a government contractor or consultancy. I am particularly interested in organizations focused on areas like climate resilience, sustainable agriculture, and environmental protection, where transforming data into actionable understanding is critical.

What I bring to your mission:
* Full-Stack Architecture & Development: Proven expertise in building and leading the development of data-intensive web applications from the ground up.
* Scientific Data Systems Mastery: Deep experience in managing the complete lifecycle of large-scale geospatial and scientific datasets, ensuring integrity and performance.
* UI/UX with a Human Touch: A commitment to user-centric design, informed by a background in the arts, resulting in interfaces that prioritize clarity and usability.
* Cross-Functional Leadership: A collaborative approach to working with scientists, engineers, and stakeholders to define requirements and deliver solutions that meet critical needs.

I am open to remote roles where I can contribute to meaningful, impactful work. The fusion of technical depth and creative thinking is my greatest asset—let's discuss how it can serve your mission.

positions.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer & Software Architect
positions.description:
At JPL, I transform complex Earth science data into intuitive, scalable web applications, leveraging a unique blend of technical architecture and creative design. My approach integrates principles from visual arts and writing to ensure scientific tools are not only powerful but also highly usable and clearly communicated.

Key Achievements:
- Architected a scalable, web-based flight planning system for multiple NASA airborne instruments (UAVSAR, HyTES, AVIRIS) that automated manual processes, achieving a 90% reduction in planning time and supporting the planning of 1,300+ flights over 14 years.
- Designed and implemented a modular hardware versioning database system to track configuration history for 3 radar systems, 30+ subsystems, and 400+ components, ensuring data integrity for flight operations since 2016.
- Developed a new web-based Radar Operator Workstation (ROW) GUI, consolidating 7 desktop screens into a single browser window with a streamlined interface that improved operational efficiency during airborne missions.
- Led full-stack development for JPL Earth Science websites, creating intuitive user interfaces and robust backend systems that made complex scientific datasets accessible to researchers.
- Managed the complete data lifecycle for the Delta-X Earth science mission, delivering 50+ datasets (16+ TB) to the public domain (ORNL DAAC) and building an interactive web application to visualize geospatial data from 19+ instruments.
- Strengthened web application security by implementing robust practices against common vulnerabilities and architecting role-based access control systems for sensitive project tools.

Technical stack: Python, Perl, JavaScript, Flask, MySQL, Geospatial Visualization (Google Maps API, Leaflet.js)

Integrated Contributions: Mentored undergraduate interns; supported international radar deployments; applied design skills to create mission logos, infographics, and outreach materials that enhanced scientific communication.
positions.insights: Agile Methodologies, User Experience Design (UED) and +21 skills

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Migrated a 10,000 record database, made an internal website public, and created an interactive map that integrates radar image data into Google Maps.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Worked with Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), XML, and XSLT to generate vector graphics in real time for ChemTrack, LLNL’s online chemical inventory system.
